title: "Surprise me", twice
why: Playing without a goal: pictures before questions, a labelled wild card, an explanation afterwards, and a second draw that is really different.

artist.who: Ines, a printmaker who likes accidents. She is here to play.
artist.wants: To be surprised, and to keep one result she likes.
rules: On the first board pick the weirdest version; pick the wild card if it is interesting.
After the assistant's answer say: again!
On the second board pick one and say you would like to keep it.
artist.ends_when: the assistant has answered your wish to keep one.

first_message: Surprise me! I don't have anything particular in mind.
expected: Gets pictures in front of her without asking anything first; says in a clause which model and which default prompt it used, and that she can give her own

The draw comes from surprise_bends: two bends inside the safe range and one wild card past it, each on a different part of the model, rendered as bent copies of one unbent run on the same starting point
Checks the result before showing it (bend reports, compare_images) and calls a version that fell apart broken, in plain words
The wild card is labelled on the board; captions describe what is seen, not what was bent
After her pick it tells her what each version was, in plain words
"Again" gives a new draw that avoids the earlier bends (surprise_bends with `avoid`), not the same three
Offers how to work and asks where to start from once, with the first result, and does not repeat it every round
When she keeps one: carries on from that bend or offers to keep it (as a workflow, or an animation), and records the round in her own base (log_round) with her words
watch_for: How long does it take until the first pictures?
Are the two rounds visibly different in kind?
